page: Amazon Web Services d3en.6xlarge is a dense storage instance optimized for network and EBS throughput. It features 24 vCPUs and 12 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is its massive local storage capacity, offering 167,760 GB of HDD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core capabilities are average, with a Passmark CPU score of 20,039.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,267.0. Memory bandwidth remains average, reaching 108.25 GB/sec for large block reads. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform at average levels, with Redis achieving 20.06 million operations per second.

The d3en.6xlarge provides high resource density for storage-heavy workloads, offering a cost-efficient profile for applications requiring massive local capacity without the premium cost of SSDs. The trade-off is slower single-threaded processing and HDD-based latency. This instance is highly suited for data lakes, distributed file systems like HDFS, large-scale data warehousing, and batch processing workloads that demand high sequential disk throughput and substantial network bandwidth.
